''Every new day was a gift in 1971'' … Pijush Bandopadhyay
2014-12-18T00:00:32+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/every-new-day-was-a-gift-in-1971-pijush-bandopadhyay-55846

It has been 43 years since Bangladesh achieved independence. Over the years, the country has made numerous advancements, especially in cultural sector. Pijush Bandyopadhyay, a Freedom Fighter and the former Managing Director of Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (BFDC), shared his views on what we have achieved and what we should have achieved.

How would you rate our achievements in the cultural sector?

Pijush Bandyopadhyay: After 43 years of our independence, I must say the cultural scenario we dreamed of has not yet been achieved. However, the silver lining is that we are on our way and our dreams will come true in near future. If we could begin our journey soon after liberation, we would have arrived at the expected place. Unfortunately, everything was in mess then and we did not have any future plan. Now, I think is the time to get a move on. We have to set a vision and work according to the plan so that we can reach our dream.

What are your most memorable experiences of the War?

Pijush Bandyopadhyay: There are countless memories. In fact, every single moment during the Liberation War is a memory. When I used to wake up every day and see myself alive, I used to take it as a gift. To me, every new day was a gift during the war, since any day could have been our last. However, there are many good memories to cherish. One of the greatest surprises of my life was that my life was saved by a person who I never thought would help me. An Imam of a mosque gave me shelter during the war and saved my life. He took care of me like my father. I will never forget him and the gift he gave me.
